observations: Photo 0: close-up of an engine's timing/pulley area, showing belt, tensioner pulleys, and bolts; no brand or model markings visible.
Photo 1: top view of an engine with wiring harness, injectors, and intake manifold; no plate, sticker, or engine code visible.
Photo 2: side view of engine block near throttle body and valve cover, with oily residue and no readable identifiers.
Watermark 'GOD OF ABRAHAM INVESTMENT' appears on all photos; it is a seller branding overlay, not proof of origin or condition.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, or displacement marking is visible in any photo.
Surfaces show grease, oil residue, and corrosion typical of a used/pulled engine; no visible cracks or breaks.

claims.claim: Dealer in all kinds of Japanese parts engine and accessories
claims.evidence: No badge, engine code, or nameplate visible in any photo to confirm Japanese make or specific model.

risks.risk: Engine make/model unknown, which drives price heavily (e.g., 4-cylinder vs V6, displacement, brand).
risks.proof: Clear photo of engine code sticker, stamped block number, or VIN/engine tag.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this; price range would be too wide to even set a worst case

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (no start-up proof).
risks.proof: Video of engine running/idling with sound.
Odometer photo from donor vehicle or import documentation.

risks.risk: Visible oil residue could indicate leaks or seep from gaskets/seals.
risks.proof: Close-up of oil pan, valve cover gasket, and crank seal areas when dry.
risks.if_unproven: priced as leaking until shown dry and clean

risks.risk: Missing accessories (starter, alternator, sensors) not clearly visible in all photos.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photos showing all ancillary parts attached.

proof_requests: Photo of engine code/model sticker or stamped number on the block.
Video of the engine running or turning over with sound.
Photo of odometer or any documentation showing mileage/origin.
Clear, dry shots of oil pan and gasket areas to check for leaks.
Full exterior shots showing all accessories (starter, alternator, compressor) attached.
response.reason: The photos show a used engine assembly with no readable brand, model, or engine code, so even a worst-case price cannot be set until the specific engine identity is confirmed.
